chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Khālid narrated from Abī al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام, who said:

The diyyah for the fetus, if its mother is struck and it falls from her womb before the soul is formed in it, is one hundred dinars, and it belongs to its heirs. And the diyyah of the deceased, if his head is cut off and his abdomen is split open, does not belong to his heirs; rather, it belongs to him apart from the heirs.

I said: What is the difference between them? He said: The fetus is a future matter whose benefit is hoped for, whereas this one has already passed and his benefit has gone. So when mutilation is done to him after his death, the diyyah for the mutilation becomes for him, not for anyone else. Hajj is performed with it on his behalf, or with it the various acts of righteousness are carried out, such as charity and other than that.

I said: If a man entered to dig for him a pit in which he would wash him, and the man became distracted while digging before him, then his shovel slipped in his hand and struck his abdomen and split it open, what is upon him? He said: If it was thus, then it is a mistake, and only expiation is upon him: the freeing of a slave, or fasting for two consecutive months, or charity to sixty poor persons, one mudd for each poor person according to the mudd of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله.

key_terms.الرُّوحُ: The soul, mentioned here in relation to fetal development.
key_terms.الْكَفَّارَةُ: Expiation required for an accidental wrongful act.
key_terms.دِيَةُ الْجَنِينِ: The blood money due for causing the loss of a fetus.
key_terms.دِيَةُ الْمَيِّتِ: The compensation connected to violating the body of a deceased person.
key_terms.دِيَةُ الْمُثْلَةِ: The indemnity for mutilation done to the dead body.
key_terms.صِيَامُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ: Fasting two consecutive months as a form of expiation.
key_terms.مُدٌّ لِكُلِّ مِسْكِينٍ: A mudd-measure of food given to each poor person.
key_terms.يُحَجُّ بِهَا عَنْهُ: The compensation is used to perform hajj on behalf of the deceased.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the diyyah of a fetus and on mutilating a deceased person in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings concerning the diyyah of a miscarried fetus and the violation of a deceased body. It explains that the fetus’s diyyah goes to its heirs, while compensation for mutilating the dead is spent on acts of devotion and charity on behalf of the deceased. It also states that accidental injury to a corpse requires kaffarah (expiation).

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5355 - Al-Husayn ibn Khalid narrated from Abu Al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as), who said:
"The diyyah (blood money) for a fetus, if its mother is struck and it is miscarried before the soul is breathed into it, is one hundred dinars, and this belongs to its heirs.
As for the diyyah of a deceased person whose head is severed and whose abdomen is cut open, it does not go to his heirs; rather, it belongs to him alone."
I asked: "What is the difference between the two cases?"
Imam (as) said: "The fetus represents a future life, and its benefit is anticipated. But the deceased has already passed away, and his benefit has ceased. Therefore, when he is mutilated after death, the diyyah for the mutilation is his alone, not for others. It is to be used to perform Hajj on his behalf or for acts of charity and other good deeds."
I then asked: "What if a man enters to dig a grave to wash the deceased, but while digging, he loses focus, and his shovel slips from his hand and strikes the abdomen of the deceased, cutting it open? What is required of him?"
Imam (as) said: "If it happened in this manner, it is considered unintentional (khata'), and he is required to perform kaffarah (expiation): to free a slave, or fast for two consecutive months, or feed sixty poor people, giving each one a mudd (a measure) according to the mudd of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family."
